what_happened: Recovered the full text of the cut app:presheaf-dictionary Reflection clause and def:behavior-presheaf from the paper repo's git history (commit b64b1ca0^, the commit before 'task 149: cut category-theory material'), and then compiled the entire clause end-to-end as a scratch probe on the first iteration after one tactic substitution. ref laws, section reflection, naturality, involution and the Equiv all type-check with zero sorries and measure [propext, Quot.sound].

The converse frame this task must consume (FrameOver.rev / TaskFrame.rev) is sited in FormalSystem/OpenLanguage/OpenReversal.lean, which is ABOVE the Semantics layer. A compiled probe proved that importing it into the Presheaf cluster trips the cluster's assert_not_exists FormalSystem.ProofSystem.Axiom guard through a ten-link chain (OpenReversal -> OpenValidity -> OpenTruth -> OpenClasses -> PlusPasting -> PlusValidity -> Semantics.Validity -> ValidityLayer -> FrameClassValidity -> ProofSystem.Axioms). Reuse therefore requires promoting the frame-level reversal block down into Semantics/, which widens file_scope beyond the single declared Reflection.lean.

Two pointers in the task description are stale. The swapUS/swapMinus families it names as 'still under review in task 608' do not exist anywhere in the tree and task 608 is absent from state.json. And the paper anchor instruction to read the Reflection clauses as COMMENTED OUT text in possible_worlds.tex cannot be followed: a later commit ('task 130 phase 1: retire pre-existing source comments and dead commented-out blocks') deleted the commented block, leaving only a one-sentence preview at line 1921. The text was recovered from git history instead.
